changes: Extended the original DATADATE calendar-year sample from 1988–1999 to 1988–2004, preserving the original start and adding five calendar years. Quarter t remains the fiscal-quarter observation; `cal_year` is its calendar year and `fmb_q` is the calendar-quarter estimator clock.

Rebuilt historical and added observations together from the exact current local datasets named by the accepted construction. The Compustat input now ends in 2007 so each 2004 quarter can receive its full t+1 through t+12 cash-flow outcome; the actuals PENDS screen and t-sample filter now extend through 2004.

Retained the accepted SAS construction, variable transformations, pooled 1st/99th winsorization, within-quarter OLS, and Stata xtfmb/Newey–West lags 3/7/11. Added only actual `e(sample)` original/added counts, last contributing calendar year, and corresponding aggregate scalars in each existing CSV table.

Checked the accepted handoff's time columns: `cal_year` is numeric calendar year; `fmb_q` is numeric calendar-quarter index; `datadate` is a numeric SAS date stored without a Stata display format. All fit diagnostics count on `cal_year`, with the original calendar-quarter unit retained for the estimator.
Added a by-year audit for conflicting Compustat GVKEY/DATADATE keys in 2000–2007. The original builder's conflict exclusion rule is retained.
limitations: I/B/E/S ACTU_EPSUS has no actual-level primary/diluted company-basis flag. Baseline therefore uses a disclosed basic/primary approximation (EPSPXQ and primary OPEPSQ), applies no unsupported annual dilution factor, and never infers basis from estimate-level PDF or value proximity. ACTU PENDS is period-end YYYYMM precision, so matching is at ticker/year/month; candidate mappings to multiple Compustat DATADATEs in the same month are excluded as ambiguous.

Future quarterly CFO/FCF per-share flows are rebased to the initial-quarter share basis with the relative Compustat AJEXQ_t/AJEXQ_k factor. This relies on Compustat’s current cumulative factor history; the ratio removes any common terminal base. The paper does not explicitly describe split rebasing for its future-flow sum, so this is a provider-supported best-effort interpretation of its per-share construction.

The physical p. 11 statement that there is “still only one firm observation per calendar quarter” appears in the return-test discussion. It is applied to the full-sample cash-flow panel by retaining the latest DATADATE among matched reports within each firm/calendar quarter before horizon eligibility; its scope for the cash-flow tests is not completely explicit.

Quarterly item #108/#90 mnemonic mapping is semantic best effort because the local catalog does not preserve the paper-vintage numeric crosswalk; current OANCFY/CAPXY YTD semantics are provider-verified.

Pooled 1st/99th percentiles and within-quarter OLS are best-effort choices where the paper is silent. The printed footnote 9 omits the usual factor of 2 in the Newey–West variance multiplier; xtfmb uses standard Newey–West inference. Only individual coefficient t-statistics are used.

The predecessor review reports that the paper's parent sample is 143,462 firm-quarters in 1988–1999 and requires sufficient Compustat, CRSP and IBES data (paper physical p. 11). The accepted cash-flow construction returns 233,822 matched parent rows for that original period and 339,422 pooled rows through 2004; it applies dated CRSP links but no stock-return availability gate, because the paper does not specify one for these cash-flow fits. The size and common-sample discrepancy remains unresolved.

The native Compustat key audit found 819 conflicting distinct GVKEY/DATADATE keys over the 1987–2007 builder window, including 326 in 2000–2007 (162 in observation years 2000–2004 and 164 in outcome years 2005–2007). The accepted construction excludes those conflicting keys after exact-row deduplication; it found no duplicate final GVKEY/DATADATE keys and no calendar year lost from 1988–2004.

For each 12-quarter fit, the pooled reconstruction adds eight originally dated 1988–1999 observations whose t+12 fiscal-quarter outcome had fallen beyond the predecessor builder's 2002 Compustat cutoff. This affects the replay's original-period N and is documented in the per-fit comparison; all requested fit periods still reach 2004.
